articles.body: Republicans are playing defense deep in their own territory as voter anger over price hikes puts more House and Senate seats in play in the midterms. New rounds of big spending, visits from Trump administration officials and private conversations among top GOP officials overseeing the battle for control of Congress reveal a party rushing to shore up red seats and states President Donald Trump won handily in 2024. In the House, the fight has expanded far outside the few-dozen seats considered the most competitive as Republicans start to unleash their massive warchest: Since Aug. 1, more than $110 million in ad bookings have gone toward Republican-held districts so red that Trump won them by double digits. In the Senate, Republicans are racing to shore up Ohio GOP Sen. Jon Husted as the Midwest struggles under the weight of Trump's tariffs and high diesel prices. Trump and Vice President JD Vance are both expected to travel to the state before the midterms to boost Husted, according to four people familiar with the matter who were granted anonymity to discuss not-yet-public plans. GOP leaders are also trying to keep a handle on contests in Iowa and Kansas — and they've quietly begun deprioritizing Georgia and even North Carolina, which a growing number of Republicans are privately bracing for Democrats to flip. “We need to stop the contagion,” said one senior GOP official, who, like others, was granted anonymity to speak candidly about the midterm landscape.   “The map is hilariously big right now,” said one national Republican pollster. Since Aug. 1, nearly two-thirds of advertising funds in House races have been booked or spent in races with GOP incumbents, according to a POLITICO analysis of data from AdImpact, which tracks political advertising. That includes nearly $18 million to embattled Rep. Max Miller in Ohio’s 7th District; $14.6 million to Texas’ 15th District where Monica De La Cruz faces a challenge from Tejano Singer Bobby Pulido; $9.6 million in Alaska where Rep. Nick Begich faces a challenge from independent Bill Hill; and millions more to other districts that Trump carried by double digits two years ago. The GOP holds a massive cash advantage over Democrats — which, for now, means they can afford to spend more broadly. Republican groups are dividing up the spending deluge in the final weeks ahead of the midterms, with Trump’s MAGA Inc. affiliated super PAC spending heavily to shore up safer red seats and deter Democrats from pushing into those races. “The voter enthusiasm [for Republican voters] is not where it needs to be but that’s where a money advantage can make a really big impact,” said Mark Bednar, a GOP strategist and former communications director for then-Speaker Kevin McCarthy. Republicans have adjusted their Senate map expectations: They’re still bullish about Maine, Michigan and New Hampshire. They’re not as optimistic about North Carolina — which Trump won in 2024 — but they are hoping to force Democrats to spend more there. Republicans are more concerned about Alaska and Texas. And their worries about Ohio have escalated amid soaring diesel prices and backlash to tariffs — challenges they’re also confronting in Texas, Iowa, Michigan and Kansas .  Already two battleground candidates have called for ends to the Iran war, pointing to the high prices: Iowa GOP Senate nominee Ashley Hinson , whose team has grown increasingly wary of the tight race and Michigan GOP Senate nominee Mike Rogers . Both Hinson and Rogers use top Trump pollster Tony Fabrizio to guide their campaigns. The White House did not respond to a request for comment on Hinson’s and Rogers’ remarks. Senior GOP operatives' own internal polling shows Trump's approval underwater in deep red states across the country. And an Iowa poll conducted last week by a Democratic-leaning pollster found Democrat Josh Turek with a one-point lead in the Senate race and Trump’s approval at 43 percent in the state he won by more than 13 percentage points in 2024, according to a copy of the poll obtained by POLITICO. “As more races come online, it very clearly is a defensive map for Republicans across the country,” said a national GOP strategist working on multiple battleground races. In Ohio, Republicans are optimistic that their attacks on former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown’s voting record are starting to break through, based on recent internal polling. But they’ve been conveying to outside groups for weeks that they need help reinforcing vulnerable incumbents like Husted. On Monday, the pro-crypto super PAC Fairshake said it planned to unleash $30 million against Brown, who was the top Democrat on the Banking Committee before losing reelection in 2024 — fueled in part by more than $40 million against him from Fairshake that year. “The stakes go far beyond one Senate seat,” Amy Natoce, a Husted campaign spokesperson, said in a statement. “Control of the Senate will determine which agenda moves forward in Washington: Sherrod Brown's out-of-touch socialist agenda, or Jon Husted’s agenda of lower taxes, a secure border, and an economy that rewards hard work.”   One Michigan Republican acknowledged the immense weight of the tariffs in races across the battleground state — including in the marquee Senate contest between Rogers and progressive Abdul El-Sayed, as well as across competitive House races. "Everywhere we go, we are getting hammered on it,” the Michigan Republican said. "It's crushing us." Even skeptical Republicans have been quietly checking in with their colleagues to see if the panic in redder territory is borne out in reality on the ground or just overblown polling. One GOP lawmaker who spoke to Hinson and her campaign team was somewhat surprised by their answers. “It’s real,” that House Republican told POLITICO. And POLITICO overheard a senior member of Kansas’ Republican party leadership complaining about their state’s tighter-than-expected race at the GOP’s midterm convention in Dallas earlier this month. GOP Sen. Roger Marshall, the person said, was in some trouble even as Republicans tried to dismiss the seriousness of his Democratic challenger, Adam Hamilton. Trump and Vance, meanwhile, continue to travel to states they won by double digits in 2024 to stump for Republican candidates, as Trump-aligned super PACs hammer the airwaves in far more red territory than blue. Recently-formed super PACs aligned with MAGA Inc. — Trump’s main spending vehicle that holds more than $400 million — have spent in 42 House districts so far, 30 defensive and 12 offensive. On average, they are spending in areas that voted for Trump by 7.9 points in 2024, according to a POLITICO analysis. The PACs are even spending in some districts Trump carried by 15 points as a way to shore up Republicans and deter Democratic advances, according to Republicans involved in the conversations. Major Republican super PACs, including the Trump aligned-super PACs and party-linked groups, have spent in more than two dozen GOP-held seats where Trump won by at least 5 points in 2024. “Republicans aren’t taking anything for granted this cycle and will deploy whatever resources necessary to protect our majorities and prevent Democrats from taking control,” RNC spokesperson Natalie Baldassarre said in a statement. The NRSC argued that “Democrats lack quality candidates and a clear path to victory,” so the party is “feigning optimism” and looking to candidates who have lost before, including Brown, “to somehow deliver [a] majority.” The NRCC said their opposition is “too broke to fight back.” The geography of the Senate map still favors the GOP this cycle: Democrats have to defend all of their seats, while flipping four Republican-held ones, to take control of the upper chamber. Republicans believe they have a real shot at flipping New Hampshire , and public polling shows Minnesota’s Senate race closer than expected, forcing Democrats to pay some minor attention to a state Kamala Harris won in 2024. And Republicans are still hopeful that their mid-decade gerrymandering push could still give them a structural advantage as they fight to defend the House. Republicans won the redistricting war that erupted last summer and will likely net at least six seats from it. But as economic concerns continue to dominate — with little relief in sight — Democrats are growing increasingly bullish. “You know, I look at places like Kansas where I never thought we’d have a chance, or South Carolina or even Mississippi, these places are longshots, but they look like they’re competitive,” Sen. John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.) said. For their part, senior Republicans have been working the problem from two ends, trying to gently persuade Trump in private conversations to back off some of his recent policy moves and wind down the war in Iran — while also organizing a wave of cash reinforcements across the growing map to try to stem the bleeding. GOP lawmakers pressed Trump officials at their Dallas convention and since then to take emergency actions around fuel prices and refinery capacity. A band of House Republicans led an unsuccessful attempt to vote on a federal gas tax suspension until after Election Day. And, over the weekend, Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) posted several direct appeals to Trump, asking why he hasn’t put an embargo on diesel exports. But many are convinced the bleeding won’t stop until voters get some relief at the pump. “The question is: How much longer can we go?” one senior House Republican said.
articles.headline: ‘We need to stop the contagion’: GOP ramps up midterms defense in Trump states

articles.body: ALL EYES ON GRACIE: Mayor Zohran Mamdani is expected to sit down with President Donald Trump at Gracie Mansion this afternoon, their third in-person meeting in less than a year and the latest wrinkle in one of the strangest relationships in American politics. Since Mamdani’s first, shockingly cordial meeting with Trump at the White House last November, political observers have scratched their heads about the democratic socialist mayor playing nice with the Republican president despite their deep disagreements on … just about everything. Ostensibly, Mamdani is putting his personal distaste for Trump aside and betting it’s best for New York City to keep things cordial so as to avoid drawing the president’s ire. But as resistance to Trump remains animating for Democrats nationally ahead of November’s midterms, Mamdani’s strategy for engaging with him stands out. Earlier today, Gov. Kathy Hochul made clear that she, for one, has no plans to meet with Trump while he’s in New York. “I speak to him on the phone whenever I need to,” she told reporters in Manhattan. Hochul, who’s facing reelection in November and tends to directly criticize Trump more frequently than Mamdani, said it was her understanding that the mayor agreed to host the president at Gracie Mansion during a previous conversation at the White House. “The mayor and [Trump] said that when he's back in town again, he would go to Gracie Mansion,” the governor said. “I don't have a Gracie Mansion to invite him to.” Still, Hochul said there’s an opportunity for Mamdani to use the Gracie confab to push Trump on releasing federal funding for New York, including for law enforcement , that she said the president’s administration has been withholding. “We have to continue fighting for what New York needs,” she said. Mamdani’s office wouldn’t say who requested today’s meeting or share specifics about the expected focus in advance, only saying the mayor will talk to Trump about “issues affecting New York City.” A Mamdani spokesperson said the mayor will elaborate on what was discussed at a post-meeting press conference that Trump isn’t expected to attend. After the appointment at Gracie, Trump is slated to meet with French President Emmanuel Macron before headlining a couple Republican fundraisers. By contrast, after his Trump tête-à-tête, Mamdani will have dinner with Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders, who’s in the city to headline a United Nations Charter event this evening that will also feature pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil, a person familiar with the plans who was granted anonymity to discuss them told Playbook. The Queens-born Trump is in town ahead of his Tuesday address to the United Nations General Assembly. Maintaining a relationship with Trump isn’t without risk for Mamdani. As Trump remains deeply unpopular amid the war in Iran and other controversies, some Democrats are privately questioning why the mayor sees a need to keep interacting with the president. But so far, Mamdani hasn’t faced any significant pushback from his hard-left base over his engagements with Trump, with leaders of the local chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America largely viewing it as the mayor acting in the city’s best interests. — Chris Sommerfeldt and Madison Fernandez  From the Capitol EYES ON AI: Hochul floated requiring safeguards like an artificial intelligence “kill switch” as part of state-level interventions to address the rapidly evolving technology. During a Monday event in Manhattan rolling out next steps for enacting the RAISE Act, New York’s landmark AI safety law that is set to go into effect in January, the governor said she’ll “look closely at additional ways to build on” the legislation — including AI kill switches “if they're deemed feasible and in the best interest of our state.” The governor in recent days has vowed to take additional AI-related actions beyond the RAISE Act, but has not specified what that might look like. Her suggestion of a kill switch comes days after California Gov. Gavin Newsom issued an executive order to explore such a requirement for AI companies’ most-advanced models. Some in the tech industry have argued implementing one is not technically feasible. Federal legislation to enact a kill switch requirement is currently stalled in Congress. When asked to expand on the prospect of requiring a kill switch, Hochul said that “all options are on the table,” but wasn’t making a commitment. “We're going to do the research and make the decisions that are thoughtful to protect New Yorkers,” she said. “We'll go as far as we need to to protect people of this state and ultimately this country in the absence of other leadership.” Read more from Madison Fernandez in POLITICO Pro . MORE BLAKEMAN MONEY: Billionaire former casino developer Steve Wynn has donated $1 million to the main super PAC supporting Republican Bruce Blakeman’s gubernatorial bid, records filed with the state Board of Elections this morning show. The committee, Strong and Safe New York, has now raised $5.3 million since July. Wynn has been a top donor to national Republican causes for over a decade. His most recent large donations in New York came last year, when he gave $361,000 to the state GOP and $500,000 to a super PAC boosting Andrew Cuomo’s mayoral bid. — Bill Mahoney FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL ENDORSEMENT CORNER: Rep. Jared Golden (D-Maine) endorsed GOP Rep. Mike Lawler in his reelection campaign in suburban New York, Golden wrote in an opinion article published Monday. Lawler is facing a tough reelection campaign against Democrat Cait Conley in one of the biggest House battlegrounds this November. The lawmakers have previously collaborated to advance the Northeast Lobsterman Protection Act, and are both members of the centrist Problem Solvers Caucus. Golden, who is not running for reelection, was one of two House Democrats to break with the party and twice vote in favor of the Republican legislative agenda earlier in September. “Mike Lawler has been a true partner to me and a friend to fishing families he will never represent,” Golden wrote. “I strongly back him, and I hope voters send him back to work. Wherever you live, find the members who pass laws with the other party, and keep them.” House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries called the cross-aisle endorsement a “smoke and mirrors ploy” that “will do nothing to change the outcome of the race.” “In desperation, [Lawler] is peddling an 11th hour endorsement from a retiring Congressmember who represents an out of town district more than 400 miles away,” Jeffries said in a statement. “Mike Lawler is an unadulterated phony who has never shown bipartisan courage when it matters.” Read more from POLITICO’s Elleiana Green . ON THE AIRWAVES: With fewer than 50 days to go before Election Day, House Democrats’ main super PAC is making its first TV ad buy in support of Conley on Monday. The House Majority PAC said it is reserving $1.2 million on cable in the Hudson Valley contest. (An additional $1.2 million is going toward fighting Republican Rep. Tom Kean Jr.’s re-election in New Jersey, which is also covered by the New York City media market.) HMP said earlier this year that it didn’t include the high-dollar NYC media market in its initial reservations because it was “prioritiz[ing] markets where rates increase significantly.” Republicans have been largely outpacing Democrats in NY-17 on the ad spending front, thanks to significant buys from super PACs backed by the president and House leadership. From the beginning of September through Election Day, the GOP has placed $15 million on ads across broadcast, cable, CTV and digital platforms, according to ad tracker AdImpact. articles.body: CHICAGO — Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker revealed Monday that he was diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes two years ago and began taking a GLP-1 medication, resulting in an 80-pound weight loss that he says has transformed his health and daily life. The disclosure marks the first time the Democrat has publicly disclosed that he has diabetes, as well as officially acknowledging that he is on GLP-1 medication, which is prescribed both for diabetes treatment and weight loss. The governor told CBS News he started taking the medication after doctors warned that he would likely need insulin for the rest of his life. Pritzker is viewed as a likely 2028 presidential candidate and has spent two years batting away questions about his visibly slimmer appearance, though he did hint at his weight loss during the Gridiron Club and Foundation’s annual white-tie dinner in Washington, D.C., earlier this year. “I’m JB Pritzker, governor of the great state of Illinois, and if you’re seeing me in person for the very first time, yes, I’m the guy who put ‘gov’ in ‘Wegovy,’” he told the high-profile crowd . The 61-year-old governor said he has struggled with his weight since childhood, dating back to when he was a 7-year-old. That’s about the time his father, Donald Pritzker, suffered a fatal heart attack at age 39 while playing tennis. President Donald Trump has made Pritzker’s weight an issue, often commenting about it in personal attacks. Asked about his weight loss during an interview with POLITICO in the spring of 2025, Pritzker said, “How about, just for health.” In Monday’s CBS interview, the governor said he closely monitored his cholesterol, triglycerides and other health markers for years because of his family history. But after becoming governor, he acknowledged the stress of leading the nation’s sixth-largest state contributed to additional weight gain. Two years ago, that concern became more urgent when doctors diagnosed him with Type 2 diabetes, he told CBS. “My doctor said, ‘Oh no, you’ll never come off of it. You’re going to have to do this the rest of your life, and I recommend that you take a GLP-1,’” Pritzker recalled about being told he’d have to take insulin. His wife, MK Pritzker, encouraged her husband to proceed on GLP-1. “I want him to be around for a really long time,” she told CBS. The governor’s office confirmed that as a result of the GLP-1, plus improved diet and exercise, Pritzker “is no longer on insulin and down to levels that indicate no diabetes/prediabetic levels." Pritzker said the effects were almost immediate. Within days, he said, he didn’t feel the appetite urges. “It was the strangest feeling.” The governor also has gained local attention for taking walks along the Lake Michigan walking path in Chicago. Along with adopting the healthy habit, it’s allowed him to talk regularly to constituents. During Monday’s interview, Pritzker side-stepped questions about whether he was running for president. “I honestly am focused on what's best for the people of Illinois,” he said. The governor also talked about being proud of Illinois' decision to cover GLP-1 medications for people with diabetes, becoming emotional describing a woman who approached him and told him access to the medication had saved her life. The announcement about his weight comes as Pritzker is taking a more prominent role in the 2026 midterms, chairing a political action committee focused on investing at least $20 million in Democratic House races. The move has added to speculation about a potential presidential bid, where the demands of a national campaign would put his health and stamina in sharper focus.

articles.body: Voters are perfectly fine supporting candidates who aren’t white men. But they do show small preferences for candidates who are younger and Christian, according to new results from The POLITICO Poll . And voters were most likely to penalize transgender candidates in hypothetical matchups, though Democrats were more likely to support them than GOP voters were. The results cast a new light on a simmering, yearslong public conversation within both parties about what it means to be electable and whether putting forward candidates of varying backgrounds is too politically risky in a close election environment. It’s a debate that defined the last open Democratic presidential primary in 2020 and is poised to play a role in 2028 too. Democrats have largely focused their debates on whether voters would accept a person of color or a woman, particularly after President Donald Trump defeated Hillary Clinton in 2016 and Kamala Harris in 2024 — while losing to Joe Biden in 2020. But the poll results suggest the characteristics voters care most about are different, shaped by frustrations over aging politicians and both new and old culture wars. “The American people, I believe, think about identity way less than the average political consultant does,” said Mike Nellis, a longtime Democratic digital strategist who advised Harris’ 2020 presidential campaign. “Obviously there are factors in society that make it harder for women and people of color to get elected, but there are plenty of incredibly talented people out there who are capable of getting over the hump on that.” To test whether demographic characteristics make a candidate more or less electable, POLITICO’s polling partner, Public First, showed thousands of respondents a series of head-to-head matchups. In each case, respondents were given basic information about the candidate’s demographics, such as their race, age and gender; their career, with titles such as doctor, attorney general or CEO; and a single-sentence description of their political alignment, either as a progressive or moderate Democratic, independent, or moderate or MAGA Republican. Respondents then picked which candidate they would prefer, and the results overwhelmingly showed voters cared the most about a candidate’s political ideology. But respondents also revealed more subtle patterns in their preferences. Voters across both parties were more likely to reject older candidates in favor of younger ones. Republicans in particular favored candidates who were described as Christian or regular churchgoers, even when controlling for the candidates’ politics. GOP respondents picked candidates described as regularly attending a church just under 9% more often than candidates who did not have any faith. That means that even though Republican respondents usually picked the GOP candidate in head-to-head matchups, for example, they were more likely to cross over and support an independent or Democratic candidate when that candidate was described as Christian. The results on sexual orientation were more complicated: When candidates were described as “gay,” they were picked about 10% less often across all voters. But when the candidate descriptions describe the candidate as a man married to his husband — without a label for sexual orientation — respondents did not pick them less often in a statistically significant manner. Voters were less likely to pick transgender candidates, with Democratic voters about 5% less likely while GOP voters were 17% less likely, all else held equal. The age results were a strong signal that voters want a new generation of candidates after the last presidential cycle was driven by concerns about Biden’s age, fueling a slew of intergenerational primary contests this year and leading major Democratic voices to publicly call for a younger candidate for 2028. Trump is now 80, and Republicans have faced their own conversations about aging politicians, as Sen. Mitch McConnell (R-Ky.) faced serious health challenges earlier this year. Amanda Litman, co-founder of Run For Something, which recruits candidates under the age of 40, said when the group started its work nearly a decade ago, younger people were often seen as “risky bets” electorally. “Now I think people are starting to see that that is not true. Voters will judge people one by one,” Litman said. “They're also really hungry for change and really hungry for someone who didn't get us into this mess.” The poll found candidates over the age of 70 were nearly 10% less likely to be picked than candidates under the age of 50, with Democrats slightly more likely than Republicans to disfavor a candidate due to age. Notably, The POLITICO Poll didn't find differences based on a candidate’s race or gender overall, outside of gender identity. That has long been a topic of debate among Democrats thinking about winning the presidency. When Harris replaced Biden on the top of Democrats’ ticket in 2024, few questioned that she would choose a white man as her running mate. Since her loss, some Democrats have argued that a white male candidate might be the best path forward for the party in 2028. Harris also wrote in her memoir about the campaign that she thought picking former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg as her running mate would have been “too risky” because he is gay, and that he otherwise would have been her ideal partner. But Buttigieg, who is contemplating running for president in 2028, recently argued that the country is ready for a gay president, saying he wouldn’t have launched a bid in 2020 otherwise. “What's on people's minds isn't about you, your identity as a candidate,” he told NBC News last weekend. “It's about them. It’s about their lives.”

articles.body: Vols veure els focs artificials de la Mercè 2026 a la platja? Aquest any hi haurà dues nits en què ho podràs fer, en el marc del XXVII Festival Pirotècnic Internacional . Els focs es llançaran a tocar de l’ espigó del Gas , però es podran veure, i gaudir, des de diferents punts del litoral, on es podran seguir els espectacles de llum, color i so. Tot seguit t’expliquem quins dies, els horaris i els millors llocs des d’on veure bé els focs artificials de la Mercè 2026 . I recorda que, a banda d’aquestes dues jornades a la platja (on el 24 de setembre hi haurà una nit de drons ), us heu d’apuntar a l’agenda el gran espectacle de focs, el Piromusical de la Mercè (27 de setembre), també a la platja, però la de la Nova Icària. >> Mercè 2026: guia completa On veure els focs artificials del Festival Pirotècnic de Barcelona? Les millors ubicacions per veure els focs artificials són just a tocar de l’espigó del Gas . Per exemple, hi ha l’opció de seguir l’espectacle des del mateix passeig Marítim de la Barceloneta – Oriol Bohigas , si bé la sorra és un dels llocs preferits per la gran majoria de ciutadans per gaudir-lo. Així, tant la platja del Somorrostro com la de la Barceloneta solen ser punts de molta afluència, ja que són a tocar de l’espigó. Ara bé, altres punts del litoral, com la platja de Sant Miquel i la de Sant Sebastià , també són bones opcions per veure l’evolució de la pirotècnia. La primera actuació omplirà de llum i color el cel barceloní de 22 a 22.20 h i anirà a càrrec de Pirotècnia FWF Concept , amb 40 anys d’experiència i vinguda des de França. articles.body: (ACN/Redacció) La Guàrdia Urbana ha detingut el raper Morad per agredir un agent. Els fets van tenir lloc diumenge passat, segons ha avançat Metrópoli i ha pogut confirmar l’ACN. articles.body: Afegeix betevé com a font preferida La Biennal de Pensament 2026 a Barcelona se celebrarà del 13 al 18 d’octubre amb el lema “Desencadenar el present” . Alguns dels noms destacats dels pensadors són: Alessandro Baricco, Lilian Thuram, Angélica Liddell, Mariana Enríquez, Wendy Brown, Patrick Radden Keefe, José Luis Guerín, Xiaolu Guo, o Chantal Maillard i Omri Boehm. Es tocaran temes com la democràcia, la guerra, les desigualtats, les migracions, les identitats i les formes de vida contemporània, amb la ciutat com a eix transversal. Aquí t’expliquem tot el que has de saber sobre la Biennal de Pensament. Biennal de Pensament 2026: quan es fa? La Biennal de Pensament d’aquest any se celebrarà del 13 al 18 d’octubre a Barcelona. L’accés és totalment gratuït . Atenció!, algunes activitats i xerrades requereixen reserva prèvia. Aquí ho podreu consultar . Temàtica i convidats de la Biennal del Pensament 2026 El lema d’enguany serà “Desencadenar el present” . Els noms destacats de l’esdeveniment seran: Mariana Enríquez (escriptora i periodista) , Angélica Liddell (dramaturga i escriptora), José Luis Guerín (director de cinema) , Lilian Thuram (exfutbolista, activista contra el racisme), Chantal Maillard (poeta i filòsofa), Eileen Truax (periodista especialitzada en migracions i fronteres), Antònia Vicens (escriptora i poeta), Jean-Philippe Kindler (artista, escriptor, comunicador i podcaster) i Fina Birulés (filòsofa i assagista). L’ara i l’aquí, a l’entorn de qüestions com la crisi de la democràcia , els autoritarismes i la solidaritat ciutadana davant dels conflictes i les amenaces contemporanis, són els eixos en què es desenvoluparà el programa d’aquesta edició. Es plantejaran preguntes com: de quina manera fomentar la solidaritat enfront dels embats del neoliberalisme? Amb quines eines la ciutat pot esdevenir un bastió de la resistència democràtica contra l’autoritarisme? Com es poden dur a terme pràctiques que millorin les condicions materials i simbòliques de la nostra vida a ciutat? Els comissaris i comissàries de l’esdeveniment són: Marina Garcés i Albert Lladó (Escola de Pensament), Elisabet Goula (CCCB), Rafael Vilasanjuan (ISGlobal) i Mireia Calafell i Berta Subirats (La Sullivan). (Al teatre del CCCB). 17.30 h: Conversa entre Omar El Akkad i Fatima Bhutto que qüestionarà el predomini dels relats occidentals i reclamarà espai per a històries, identitats i experiències tradicionalment silenciades. (A la plaça Joan Coromines). 19 h: Elaine Vilar Madruga i Anna Starobinets, en conversa amb Maria Isern , exploraran com el malson, la distopia i els cossos en transformació permeten observar les formes de control i vulnerabilitat de la vida contemporània. (A la plaça Joan Coromines). 20.30 h: Juan Evaristo Valls Boix i Anna Pacheco, amb Alba Riera , analitzaran la cultura del rendiment, la precarietat i els imaginaris de descans i desconnexió que qüestionen la centralitat productiva de la feina. (A la plaça Joan Coromines). Casa Orlandai – inici del cicle de la Xarxa de Centres Cívics de Barcelona 18 h: Els estereotips generacionals, amb Sol Picó, Montse Barderi i Alba Lafarga l 19.30 h: La resposta de les arts als discursos d’odi, amb Paula Artés, Las Huecas i Març Llinàs . Gustavo Gili 18 h: Barcelona = (diversitat + intensitat) x complexitat 15 d’octubre Hivernacle del Parc de la Ciutadella 18 h: Eileen Truax i Ainhoa Nadia Douhaibi Arrazola posaran en relació l’enduriment de les polítiques migratòries als Estats Units i a Europa. 19.30 h: Blanquitud, pensament i dret a la ciutat. la Model 18 h: Miquel Ramos, Youssef M. Ouled i Montse Santolino amb Laura Aznar examinaran com l’extrema dreta disputa els imaginaris, els afectes i el sentit comú, i com transforma els marcs amb què es parla de migració, seguretat, habitatge o desigualtat. 19.30 h: Lectura dramatitzada de les converses entre Susan Sontag i John Berger. Sobre la digitalització de les economies urbanes, la informalitat, l’habitatge, les absències familiars, la regeneració dels ecosistemes, la pertinença, els cossos i les estratègies de supervivència en entorns urbans desiguals. (A l’auditori del CCB). 12 h: Sessió per a estudiants sobre el futur d’Àfrica. (Al Pati de les Dones). 18 h: Nous vocabularis per a les ciutats del Sud Global. (Al Pati de les Dones). 19.30 h: Felwine Sarr , la revolució dels imaginaris. (Al Pati de les Dones). 21.15 h: La gran cacería , de Juan Mayorga , una peça sobre violència colonial, memòria i les contradiccions del relat europeu. (Al Teatre del CCCB). plaça Major de Nou Barris 10 h: L’obra de George Orwell 1984 articularà una activitat per a joves sobre veritat i manipulació digital. 18 h: José Luis Guerín proposarà una cartografia construïda des dels límits, els espais de pas i les històries que queden fora del relat oficial. 19.30 h: Valentín Roma i Valerio Rocco abordaran les tensions entre representació cultural, institucions i capacitat d’acció. Hivernacle del Parc de la Ciutadella 18 h: Els videojocs i les plataformes digitals es presentaran com a espais de disputa cultural, aprenentatge, captura de dades i construcció de vincles, amb una atenció especial a la infància i la joventut. 19.30 h : joventuts per a la justícia climàtica, lluites locals i internacionalistes. la Model 18 h: Ray Brassier, Eudald Espluga i Tatiana Llaguno . Sessió sobre la precarietat, la hiperconnexió i les possibilitats d’una pràctica política col·lectiva. 19. 30 h: Jean-Philippe Kindler, Marta Echaves i Adrià Porta qüestiona la conversió dels problemes socials en responsabilitats individuals i recuperen la lluita de classes com a marc d’anàlisi. 17 d’octubre CCCB- Pati de les Dones 11.30 h: Julián Casanova i Xavier Domènech, amb Sílvia Marimon , revisaran les disputes i els silencis que continuen envoltant la Guerra Civil i el franquisme. 13 h: Victoria Szpunberg, Israel Solà i Juan Mayorga analitzaran el paper del teatre en la construcció democràtica i en la preservació de la memòria. 17 h: Omri Boehm i Jordi Graupera exploraran les possibilitats i els límits d’una ètica universal basada en la dignitat humana. 18.30 h: Sofia Andrukhóvitx, Volodymyr Yermolenko, Tetyana Ogarkova i Margaryta Yakovenko , que abordaran el paper de l’escriptura davant la destrucció i l’amenaça de l’oblit. 20 h: Patrick Radden Keefe i Judit Carrera traslladaran la mirada a les estructures de poder i diners opacs del Londres contemporani. La Sedeta 12.30 h: Taula de diàleg sobre Gaza a partir de la pregunta de com se sostenen la ciutat i la vida sota condicions de destrucció i ocupació colonial. 16 h: Tau Luna conduirà un taller per repensar la ciutat des dels marges, en un exercici especulatiu de disseny urbà. 18.30 h: Míriam Cano i Laura Camargo analitzaran el llenguatge polític i les estratègies narratives de l’extrema dreta. Parc de les Glòries 12.30 h: Pòdcast Amiga date cuenta abordarà el tema del fracàs. 18 h: Fina Birulés, Wendy Brown i Begonya Saez Tajafuerce parlaran sobre la llibertat. 21 h: Oye Sherman, Shaun Debnath, Alba Segarra i Judit Martín traçaran un autoretrat humorístic de Barcelona. 22.15 h : SVSTO tancarà la jornada amb un concert que combinarà sàtira, cultura de club i crítica a la ciutat aparador. 18 d’octubre – Jornada de clausura La Sedeta 12.30 h: Taller Invisibilitats, conduït per Grigri , explorarà les fronteres i els vincles que travessen els barris però que no sempre resulten visibles. La proposta passarà de la conversa a la pràctica col·lectiva i relacionarà experiències procedents de l’Àfrica i de la península Ibèrica. CCCB- Pati de les Dones 11.30 h: Maryam Madjidi i Youssef El Maimouni conversaran sobre diàspora, classe social, contradiccions assimilació de la i les promesa meritocràtica. 13 h: Xiaolu Guo, Xisi Sofia Ye Chen i Carles Prado Fonts abordaran la relació entre llengua, memòria i migració des de dues experiències generacionals del desplaçament. 18 h: Mariana Enríquez i Valerie Miles protagonitzaran una conversa sobre la ciutat nocturna, l’arquitectura, la memòria i les històries que emergeixen quan la ciutat deixa de ser únicament un espai funcional. 19.30 h: Cloenda: acte de producció pròpia que reuneix algunes de les escriptores més destacades del present, com són Leila Guerriero, Marta Sanz, Neige Sinno, Antònia Vicens o Pol Guasch. articles.body: (ACN) Pimec Comerç proposa que la xarxa de supermercats assequibles de Barcelona anunciada per l’alcalde Collboni aprofiti el comerç de proximitat existent a la capital catalana. La patronal recorda que Barcelona ja disposa d’una xarxa de comerços, mercats municipals, pimes, professionals autònoms i cooperatives que pot contribuir a facilitar l’accés de la ciutadania a productes essencials. “Abans d’impulsar nous establiments amb suport públic, cal explorar mecanismes perquè els comerços existents puguin formar part de la xarxa de botigues assequibles, garantint unes condicions de competència equilibrades i les mateixes regles de joc per a tots els operadors”, ha defensat la presidenta de Pimec Comerç, Mònica Gregori. També et pot interessar Sorpresa i recel dels comerços de barri davant l’anunci de supermercats públics a Barcelona Andrea Cuerva Bonich 3 minuts de lectura Ajudes per al comerç de proximitat per oferir productes més assequibles “Compartim la necessitat de garantir l’accés a productes essencials a preus assequibles i defensem que el comerç de proximitat ha de formar part de la solució”, ha insistit Gregori. “Cal aprofitar el teixit comercial establert als nostres barris i buscar fórmules de col·laboració que permetin assolir aquest objectiu sense generar una xarxa paral·lela als nostres establiments de proximitat existents”, ha posat sobre la taula la presidenta de Pimec Comerç, que també avisa que cal actuar sobre els factors que condicionen el preu final i no focalitzar el problema en el comerç de proximitat. “Especialment en el cas dels aliments frescos , el preu respon a costos que es generen al llarg de tota la cadena de valor, com els de producció, transport, energia i personal, així com les càrregues administratives, mentre que molts establiments treballen amb marges molt ajustats”, ha reflexionat en veu alta la presidenta de Pimec Comerç, que igualment considera que els recursos municipals vinculats a la iniciativa podrien servir per facilitar que els comerços existents ofereixin determinats productes en condicions més assequibles, a través de fórmules de col·laboració i suport que caldria definir conjuntament amb el sector. També et pot interessar Barcelona crea un fons per comprar comerços “emblemàtics i estratègics” en risc de desaparèixer Ester Magdaleno Helena Molist Sancho 2 minuts de lectura Diagnosi de l’oferta comercial i transparència sobre les condicions del projecte En paral·lel, en aquelles zones on sigui necessari ampliar l’oferta comercial, Pimec Comerç planteja mesures com lloguers assequibles, incentius específics , suport al relleu generacional i la reducció de barreres d’entrada. “El comerç de proximitat va molt més enllà de la seva funció comercial perquè genera activitat econòmica i ocupació, contribueix a la cohesió social i dona vida als carrers”, ha valorat el president de Pimec Barcelona, Àlex Goñi, que ha alertat de les dificultats que travessa actualment el comerç alimentari de proximitat a Barcelona. Abans del desplegament del projecte, Pimec Comerç exigeix que es faci una diagnosi de l’oferta comercial i de les necessitats de les zones on es preveu actuar, que permeti identificar els establiments existents que podrien participar en la iniciativa i detectar aquells barris on sigui necessari reforçar l’oferta comercial. Finalment, la patronal demana transparència sobre les condicions econòmiques i de gestió del projecte i veu imprescindible que el sector comercial participi en el disseny, seguiment i avaluació de la iniciativa de la xarxa de supermercats assequibles.

articles.body: Les Festes de la Mercè 2026 ja són aquí i, per tant, augmenta el risc de pluja . I és que estadísticament ens trobem en un període en què veure ploure a Barcelona és força probable. De fet, la probabilitat de veure ploure per la Mercè a la ciutat és a l’entorn d’un de cada quatre anys . Però, què diuen els models per a enguany? La previsió del temps marca que podríem tenir moments de tot , especialment tranquils, amb sol i calor, però amb tendència a l’augment dels núvols en el tram final. També et pot interessar La Mercè 2026 a Barcelona: Programa en PDF, concerts, Piromusical i portes obertes de la festa major Neus Valls Núria Dias Sílvia Carbonell 9 minuts de lectura La Mercè 2026, molt estiuenca però amb un possible gir en el tram final Tot i que aquest moment clau del calendari barceloní arriba amb la tardor ja estrenada, enguany els termòmetres i el calendari continuaran anant per lliure. Això sí, són dates especialment sensibles: la probabilitat de pluja a la ciutat ronda el 25 % . I és aquí on entra la llegenda de les llàgrimes de Santa Eulàlia : es diu que quan plou per la Mercè no són només gotes, sinó les llàgrimes de l’antiga patrona de Barcelona, trista perquè la Mare de Déu de la Mercè li va prendre protagonisme. Aquesta història popular , amb els anys, ha convertit la pluja de setembre en un dels clàssics més entranyables del calendari barceloní. També et pot interessar On i quan veure els concerts gratis de Love of Lesbian, La Pegatina i Svetlana per la Mercè 2026 Eva Vial 2 minuts de lectura Tot fa pensar en una primera part de la Mercè plàcida, tranquil·la, assolellada i, sobretot, càlida . Esperem un altre pic de calor coincidint amb aquest dijous, 24 de setembre, a Barcelona i a la resta de l’entorn metropolità. Encara que la nit i la matinada seran suaus arran de mar i amb un punt de fresca al prelitoral, les màximes anotaran més de 30 ºC a la ciutat i fins a 32 o 33 ºC al prelitoral . Farà sol o estones de ressol especialment a partir de la tarda, amb l’arribada d’un tel de núvols prims. Bombolla càlida i, a més, reforçada per un vent de garbí que tornarà a bufar reforçat i reescalfat amb ràfegues puntualment superiors als 40 km/h. En aquest sentit, des de dimecres, 23, fins divendres, 25 de setembre, el temps respectarà qualsevol activitat a l’aire lliure . Faríeu bé d’anar vestits amb roba lleugera pròpia de l’estiu, amb el permís d’alguna jaqueta fina al final del dia i de matinada. Ara bé, encara que l’ambient podria seguir sent tranquil, és probable que els núvols vagin a més i el cel sigui més deslluït la tarda de dissabte i diumenge. Encara que el risc per pluja ara mateix es manté baix, l’arribada d’un front en el tram final de la Mercè podria deixar-nos algun ruixat esporàdic o gotellada . A més, la calor podria perdre pistonada progressivament. Encara és aviat per fer sonar les campanes: la previsió del temps manté certa incertesa i, ara com ara, no permet donar res per fet.
